author: A Robot
objectives: Explain the importance of antiparallel orientation.
Trace the enzymatic functions of helicase, polymerase, and ligase during replication.
Articulate the semiconservative model of DNA replication.

modules.description: Introduction to DNA structure: from ladder to double helix.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Identify the sugar-phosphate backbone and nitrogenous bases.
Understand the transition from schematic to 3D helix.
instructions: Watch the transition to the double-helix form.

clips.changeMeaning: Initialize the scene with a 2D ladder representation of DNA.
clips.narration: DNA is a polymer with a repeating sugar-phosphate backbone and nitrogenous bases that project inward, pairing with their complements.

clips.changeMeaning: Transition the ladder into a 3D double helix.
clips.narration: The molecule naturally twists into this iconic double helix. Each turn spans about ten base pairs.

modules.description: Exploring antiparallel orientation and 5' to 3' directionality.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Explain the antiparallel orientation of DNA strands.
Relate 5'-to-3' directionality to the carbon atoms in the sugar ring.
instructions: Rotate the helix to inspect the 5' and 3' terminal labels.

clips.changeMeaning: Add directional arrows and 5'/3' labels to the helix.
clips.narration: The strands are antiparallel: one runs 5' to 3', the other 3' to 5'. This is forced by the chemical orientation of the sugar-phosphate backbone.

modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Understand the difference in hydrogen bond counts between base pairs.
instructions: Drag matching nitrogenous bases from the palette to complete the complementary DNA strand.

clips.changeMeaning: Clear the right side base pairs for student interaction.
clips.narration: Drag bases from the palette to complete the strand. Remember: A pairs with T, G with C. Watch the hydrogen bond indicators.

modules.description: The initiation of DNA replication at the replication fork.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Trace the actions of helicase and single-strand binding proteins.
Understand why strands must be kept separate during synthesis.
instructions: Observe the unwinding process and the stabilization by SSBs.

clips.changeMeaning: Introduce helicase and begin unwinding the DNA helix.
clips.narration: Helicase unwinds the double helix, breaking hydrogen bonds to expose template strands for replication.

clips.changeMeaning: Attach single-strand binding proteins to the exposed strands.
clips.narration: Single-strand binding proteins stabilize the exposed strands, preventing them from snapping back together.
